items.summary: api-side: split toolkit ActionRef string→Ref{module,type,id} defensively (TakeAction wave)
items.details: The TakeAction contract (PR #171/v0.1.100) carries action_ref as a proto Ref{module,type,id}, but the toolkit emits it as a colon-delimited string via core.Ref.String() (core/ref.go:81 = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:%s", Module,Type,ID)), e.g. dnd5e:combat_abilities:attack. rpg-api parses string→Ref at translate by splitting on ':'. Toolkit (verified both publish paths) confirms it's ALWAYS a clean triple in practice — the web sends full triples, tests confirm. EDGE (toolkit-flagged, defensive only): a malformed caller with empty Module/Type yields '::attack' (colon-delimited, empty parts). api's split should TOLERATE/VALIDATE a short or empty-part split rather than panic/index-out-of-range. NOT a proto-shape issue (the wire field is a clean Ref); purely an api-consumer parse-robustness note. Routed to the api lane via team-lead 2026-06-01. Not blocking — no real caller produces it.

items.summary: EncounterService carries TWO state shapes — verified at file:line
buf breaking is `continue-on-error: true` in CI — single-line fix
~5,154 lines of unused proto across 5 services + 4 deprecated RPCs
Position is currently `double X/Y/Z`, slated for int32 breaking change
items.details: api/v1alpha1/room_common.proto:9 — Position uses `double x = 1; double y = 2; double z = 3;`. Per rpg-project/ideas/coordinate-types/design.md, this needs to move to int32 to match the cube coordinate invariant (X+Y+Z=0) used by the dungeon component. The double signature is the root cause of the int↔float64 casts that produced 5 coordinate bugs in Round 2 (rpg-api PRs #459, #461, #463, #466, #467). Breaking wire change; design says rpg-api types must land first. Likely v1alpha2 package bump rather than in-place edit.

items.summary: Two dead messages in CharacterService with no RPC backing them
items.details: character.proto:364 UpdateCharacterRequest + line 374 UpdateCharacterResponse — no `rpc UpdateCharacter` exists (verified by grep). Section-based updates (UpdateName/UpdateRace/UpdateClass/etc) replaced bulk updates. Same pattern at line 509 UpdateDraftRequest + line 519 UpdateDraftResponse — no `rpc UpdateDraft`. Both define `repeated string update_mask` for a field-mask pattern that was never wired. Removable without consumer impact. Worth bundling into issue #140 cleanup.

items.summary: Deprecated fields catalog — TurnState, Proficiencies, DamageComponent
items.details: TurnState (encounter.proto:223): movement_used (line 225), movement_max (226), action_used (227), bonus_action_used (228), reaction_available (229) — all `[deprecated = true]`, superseded by ActionEconomy. PLUS reserved 9, 10 for retired disengage_active/dodge_active. Proficiencies (character.proto:286): armor field 3 (line 306) and weapons field 4 (line 309) — both `[deprecated = true]`, superseded by armor_categories/weapon_categories/specific_weapons. DamageComponent (encounter.proto:510): source field 1 (line 512) — `[deprecated = true]`, superseded by SourceRef source_ref. ChoiceSubmission (choices.proto:165): the oneof selection (line 178) is comment-deprecated (no field option), superseded by selection_ids field 5. EquipmentSlot.EQUIPMENT_SLOT_GLOVES (character.proto:1180) is rejected at runtime by rpg-api but has no proto-level deprecation marker — enum-value deprecation has no examples in the repo.

Verified by grepping `^message <name>` across all .proto files. (1) Room — api.v1alpha1.Room (room_common.proto:176, generic, unused) vs dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.Room (encounter.proto:111, live). (2) Entity — api.v1alpha1.Entity (room_common.proto:33, unused) vs dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.EntityState/EntityPlacement (encounter.proto:18, 45). (3) EntitySize — dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.EntitySize (enums.proto:818) vs sandbox.api.v1alpha1.EntitySize (sandbox_common.proto:73) — same six values, different fully-qualified names. (4) DiceRoll — api.v1alpha1.DiceRoll (dice.proto:49, result form) vs dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.DiceRoll (common.proto:45, notation form) — both LIVE, different shapes, same name; this is the worst collision. (5) ValidationResult — api.v1alpha1.ValidationResult (room_common.proto:216, generic) vs dnd5e.api.v1alpha1.ValidationResult (common.proto:122, three-tier). Plus Wall vs WallSegment between api.v1alpha1 and sandbox.api.v1alpha1.

items.summary: Three pagination patterns coexist in the repo
items.details: Pattern A (AIP-158 inline, the standard): page_size + page_token + next_page_token + total_size on the request/response directly. Used by every live list RPC in CharacterService. Pattern B (event-style): GetEncounterHistory (encounter.proto:386, 397) uses `limit` / `up_to_event_id` / `has_more` / `last_event_id` — different field names from Pattern A. Pattern C (PageInfo envelope): unused services in api/v1alpha1 use `PageInfo page_info` from room_common.proto:223. The three coexist; Pattern A is the de facto standard.

items.summary: Three error patterns coexist in the repo
items.details: Pattern A (dominant): `bool success = 1; string error = 2;` — used by OpenDoorResponse, EquipItemResponse, ShortRestResponse, LongRestResponse, AttackResponse, ActivateCombatAbilityResponse, ExecuteActionResponse. Pattern B (one-off): `MovementError` typed-error message (encounter.proto:419) with enum + string + map<string,string> — only used by MoveCharacterResponse, which is itself deprecated. Pattern C: gRPC status codes (codes.Unimplemented for GetCombatState). Pattern A is the de facto standard.

items.summary: buf breaking config is `use: [FILE]` (more sensitive than PACKAGE)
items.details: buf.yaml line 7-9: `breaking: use: [FILE]`. This means changes are flagged per-file, not per-package. Stricter than the default PACKAGE setting. Implication for the Position int32 migration: it must be a NEW file (v1alpha2 package) rather than an in-place edit of room_common.proto.

items.summary: Lint config excepts PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX and RPC_RESPONSE_STANDARD_NAME
items.details: buf.yaml lint.except includes PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX (we use v1alpha1 style; default would force v1alpha) and RPC_RESPONSE_STANDARD_NAME (streaming RPCs use event-style names like EncounterEvent). Two intentional deviations from the buf default lint set. New deviations should land in a discussed PR, not added quietly.

items.summary: C++ generation runs in CI but no UE consumer exists
items.details: buf.gen.yaml lines 22-28 generate C++ via buf.build/protocolbuffers/cpp + buf.build/grpc/cpp into gen/cpp. No UE consumer in this workspace exercises it. Makefile has `package-ue-plugin` and `validate-ue-plugin` targets (per old docs/P001-ue-cpp-client-generation.md, now archived). Decision pending: keep generating speculatively, or remove the C++ plugins from buf.gen.yaml until a real UE consumer materializes.

items.summary: PR #136 is the worked example for breaking-change discipline
items.details: PRs #135/#136 (2026-04-03) introduced unified entity state and retired the legacy fragmented event fields. The retirement was done correctly: every retired field has both `reserved <number>` and `reserved "<name>"`. Example at encounter.proto:903-905 (CombatStartedEvent reserves 1-5 with names). This is the model to replicate when retiring fields. The team knows the discipline; CI just doesn't enforce it (issue #139).
